text:
You really need to have the 3060 TI in the mix  due o it having a 256 bit memory bus width like the Intel Arc models better than the 3060 and much better than the 4060 with it's pathetic 128 bit bus.
The same applied with previous generations where the 12 Gig variants used a narrow memory bus compared to the Super 2060 and 3060 TI both of which whilst 8 Gig memory ran the wider more efficient Bus width that  in the real world compensates over the greater memory available in most real world scenarios.

Intel were very clever in realising the Memory Bandwidth matters more than most realise and that probably comes from the CPU division where high end HEDT Systems used triple and later quad channel ram compared to Normal Mainstream CPU with only dual channel Ram.

Then we have the scenario of when Laptops started going to soldered ram many at the same time dropped  even Dual Chanel support and people need to realise those bottlenecks do matter

text:
Great to see the video. :) I agree about the Arc cards being much better video editing cards now than they were last year and I have been enjoying the Premiere Pro 24 beta even more in that respect.

One thing I wanted to point out though is that you can already see a benefit in Premiere Pro 23 to using an Arc card with a UHD770 iGPU, especially in the processing 4K h.264 part of the PugetBench results. Here’s what I got on my system when pairing a 13900K with that iGPU and an Arc A770 16GB.

Arc A770 alone: 205.09 fps
A770+UHD770: 237.12 fps

A great combo for Premiere Pro that scored even higher in standard overall on my system than a 4070+UHD770 combo (though lower than the 6800 XT+UHD770 or 7800 XT+UHD770 combo).

Like you said, both the UHD770 and Arc series outperform the AMD iGPUs - but the best PugetBench video editing scores I’ve gotten with cards under $600 so far have been with AMD discrete GPUs + Intel iGPUs. They make a fantastic combo.

Also, the 7800 XT showed massive improvement in 4K h.264 to h.264 footage in DaVinci Resolve 18.6.

6800 XT (iGPU disabled): 109.96
7800 XT (iGPU disabled): 192.19

text:
The Unreal Engine performance isn’t on the level of the video editing performance at this point - but Unreal Engine 4 performance does seem to be better than a 3060. I did a mixture of 3D modeling, game engine and video testing and the video editing was definitely the best part of the Arc experience - especially for decoding 4K and 8K h.264 footage in Premiere Pro on Intel processors with an iGPU. Unfortunately I haven’t gotten to Unreal Engine 5.3 yet - installed it on the test system yesterday.

However, setting aside Unreal engine specifically, if you look at games like F1 22 you can get a sense of where things are heading as driver support improves for Arc in various engines. In contrast to Forza Horizon 5 (which had an unexpectedly high number of issues), I found the Arc A770 16GB in F1 22 offered the sort of performance at higher resolutions I would expect from a 3060 or 4060.

In 4K h.264 decoding in particular…

3060 12GB: 106.2 fps
3060 + UHD770: 196.19 fps
4070: 112.32 fps
4070 + UHD770: 201.82
Arc A770 16GB: 205.09 fps
